document.description: An eligible Australian visa can support simplified visitor entry on qualifying itineraries.

unlocks.conditions: Hold a passport from China or one of the Pacific Islands Forum countries listed by Immigration New Zealand. Enter Australia through immigration, depart directly from an Australian airport, and hold an eligible Australian visa valid at check-in and a valid New Zealand Electronic Travel Authority (NZeTA).
unlocks.additionalRequirements: Check your Australian visa subclass against the official list. Request the NZeTA at least 72 hours before travel. Transit through Australia without entering the country does not qualify.

source.pageSection: October 2026 update; Who can apply; Pacific Islands Forum countries; Eligible Australian visas

unlocks.notes: An NZeTA authorizes travel. When entry permission is granted, Immigration New Zealand can issue a Visa Waiver Visitor Visa at the border for up to three months at a time. Multiple trips are possible on a valid NZeTA when each trip satisfies the direct travel requirement.

unlocks.conditions: Ordinary passport holders from China or India may visit Peru for tourism or business without a Peruvian visa if their Australian visa has at least six months of remaining validity.
unlocks.additionalRequirements: Present the qualifying Australian visa and an ordinary passport with at least six months of validity when entering Peru. Follow the stay authorized on admission.

source.pageSection: Temporary tourist visa exemption for Chinese and Indian nationals

additionalSources.pageSection: Visa exemption and authorized stays for Chinese and Indian passport holders

unlocks.notes: The 180-calendar-day ceiling covers a continuous or multiple successive visits. The period is six months for Chinese passport holders under Decree 069-2016-RE and one year for Indian passport holders under Decree 006-2017-RE.
